lesson.scenario: A gateway shapes a burst through a bounded FIFO bucket that leaks exactly two requests per second.
entities: Buffers at most five admitted requests
Emits one drain tick every 500 milliseconds
Records queue drops and shaped throughput

steps.title: First arrivals queue
steps.narration: Three simultaneous requests enter an empty FIFO bucket.
steps.outcome: The burst is absorbed without changing the configured outlet rate.
steps.invariant: Accepted requests retain FIFO order inside the bucket.

steps.title: Bucket reaches capacity
steps.narration: Three more requests arrive before a leak tick; two fit and the sixth overflows.
action: enqueue r4,r5; reject r6 at t=0.1
steps.outcome: The bounded bucket converts excess burst load into an explicit rejection.
steps.invariant: Queue depth never exceeds five; overflow is rejected rather than hidden in unbounded memory.

steps.title: First leak tick
steps.narration: At 0.5 seconds the clock releases exactly the oldest request.
steps.outcome: One unit of queue capacity opens while output remains evenly spaced.
steps.invariant: A tick removes at most one request regardless of how many are waiting.

steps.title: New work joins the tail
steps.narration: A later request uses the newly opened slot behind all older work.
steps.outcome: The limiter admits new work only when a prior tick creates capacity.
steps.invariant: Later arrivals cannot bypass requests already buffered.

steps.title: Constant drain continues
steps.narration: Ticks at 1.0 and 1.5 seconds release r2 and r3, independent of arrival burst size.
steps.outcome: The outlet observes a smooth two-request-per-second stream.
steps.invariant: The leaky bucket enforces a constant service cadence and does not preserve burst throughput.

production.scenario: City operators in us-east-1 push a stadium-event surge override batch, and the pricing admin API must drain writes into the downstream pipeline at a smooth fixed rate.
components: submits surge override batches for Manhattan and Brooklyn
owns fare override writes for the regional pricing stack
publishes per-city drain contracts and emergency caps
smooths admitted override traffic into the writer lane
authoritative sink consumed by pricing materializers
stores shard ownership and restart checkpoints
stores shed batches consumed by overflow analysis tooling and on-call dashboards
flows: City ops pushes a burst of 600 overrides ahead of a stadium event.
The API loads the active 40 rps contract and overflow threshold before admitting work.
The control plane updates the gate for the current city and deployment epoch.
request admission for batch FO-771 on shard nyc-a
The batch is handed to one limiter shard instead of going straight to the writers.
Admitted records leave at the configured steady rate so downstream writers stay stable.
Ownership and replay position are checkpointed so a restarted pod can resume safely.
emit shed notice for FO-771 overflow
If backlog crosses the emergency cap, overflow is recorded for replay rather than silently dropped.
